fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to improve visibility at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back overhanging branches above the access drive to allow full vehicle height clearance for fire and rescue apparatus.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so emergency vehicles can reach both structures.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the detached structure so emergency vehicles do not have to back out to the road.
• Mark a secondary staging area on the open lawn where emergency vehicles can park without blocking the access drive.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move on foot between the two buildings.
• Keep the walkway clear of obstructions so responders can move quickly between structures on foot.
• Notify your local fire department of the single access point and limited turnaround space so they can note it in pre-incident planning records.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs and brush growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure's exterior walls.
• Cut grass around the structure short and keep it cut short, especially during dry periods.
• Clear brush growing along both sides of the driveway to allow emergency vehicles to pass through without obstruction.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles can move through freely.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrubs and brush areas near the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the structure so there is open ground between individual plants and the building.
• Separate large trees near the structure from nearby shrubs and brush by removing the low-growing vegetation beneath and around them.
• Keep the single driveway access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and other debris at all times.
• Thin trees and brush along the driveway edges so the route stays visible and passable from both directions.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure up to a height that keeps them clear of shrubs and brush below.
